messages:
elaine: Quick question — Acme wants to run a Dedicated POC but will only open their firewall to short-lived IPs. They asked for a TTL-based static IP or a proxy approach. Can we support a short-lived static IP (e.g., 24h) or do we recommend proxying?

mike: We can support two patterns for POCs: long-lived EIP per-customer (standard) or an ephemeral NAT pool that we rotate (24h/48h). Ephemeral requires us to share the new IPs each rotation. Pricing note: Dedicated capacity is billed as usual, but we can offer a POC discount and include ephemeral egress as part of the onboarding.

sam: Tech details: ephemeral pool = lower commitment but operational overhead (we push rotated list to customer). If they need a one-off short window, proxying through a customer-dedicated proxy (mTLS) is cleaner.

sam: Quick example rotation script we use internally (very small):
```
# rotate-egress.sh (pseudo)
ALLOC=$(aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc)
ASSOC=$(aws ec2 associate-address --allocation-id $ALLOC --instance-id i-xxxxxx)
# update internal list + notify customer via webhook
```

tanya: If firewall team is strict, suggest proxy + mTLS. That avoids having to update rules every day. We have a runbook with cert rotation snippets: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/networking/poc-proxy (internal).

elaine: One more: can the hosted API key be scoped so the key only talks to their Dedicated pool/model? Customer wants isolation so keys from other tenants won't work.

mike: Yes — we can issue an API key scoped to the tenant/dedicated-instance with per-key rate limits. We'll note that the key still needs to be rotated and logged. For the POC, we can issue a short-lived key (TTL) too.

sam: Onboarding checklist for this flow (short):
- Customer provides CIDR(s) or accepts our ephemeral pool webhook.
- Decide proxy vs ephemeral NAT.
- Confirm cert model (our certs vs BYOC). BYOC adds ~2 business days.
- Specify API key scope and TTL.

mike: Firewall snippet we usually send customers (examples):
```
# allow outbound to Redwood POC NATs (example)
allow from <your-hosts> to 52.86.12.0/24 port 443 proto tcp
# DNS allowed for SNI
allow to *.redwood-inference.com
```

elaine: Great — I'll send both options (ephemeral NAT + proxy) and a short pricing note. Any enterprise/legal blockers we should flag?

mike: Only big blockers are full compliance needs (SOC2/HIPAA) — if they require that level, Private/VPC or on-prem will be required and that's a separate engagement. Otherwise, Dedicated POC + ephemeral/proxy is fine.

deploy-bot: New issue created: INF-2345 — POC ephemeral egress setup request (assignee: sam)

elaine: Perfect, thanks all. I'll loop in customer with the two patterns and ask for CIDR or approval for webhook updates. :thumbsup:
